title: Basic Homemade Applesauce
ingredients: 3 to 4 lbs apples (about 6 to 8 medium); mix sweet and tart, like McIntosh, Fuji, Gala or Honeycrisp with Granny Smith
instructions: Prep the apples: Peel, core, and chop the apples into roughly 1-inch chunks. Leaving peels on gives a pinker sauce, but the finished sauce must then go through a food mill or high-powered blender to remove skin fragments.

Simmer: In a large pot, combine the apple chunks, liquid, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are completely tender and easily mashed with a fork.
Mash or blend: Remove from heat. For chunky texture, mash the apples in the pot with a potato masher. For silky-smooth texture, use an immersion blender, food processor, or standard blender.
Season and finish: Stir in the cinnamon, vanilla extract, and sweetener to taste. Serve warm, or chill in the refrigerator before serving.
notes: Serving = about 2/3 cup (recipe yields ~4 cups); nutrition is an estimate per serving, assuming peeled apples, water as the liquid and no added sweetener. Each tbsp of sugar adds ~8 kcal and ~2g sugar per serving.
